title: arXiv Table 5 -- exact Gillespie SSA cost, published real-world models
revision: 2026-08-20: samoilov_futile_cycle runs the curated record's own horizon, t_end=10 with n_steps=2000 (Fig. 3A), replacing t_end=0.0018, which was chosen for the superseded 6/6 artifact (lanl/bngsim#425). B10's cost moves by about four orders of magnitude. Prior revision 2026-08-19: the 8 BNGL rows are re-pointed at the curated BNGL-Models records (wshlavacek/BNGL-Models @6783b6e9) and share one generated .net set with the psa suite at ../../models/net/curated/, regenerated by benchmarks/models/regenerate_curated_nets.py. Sizes that moved: gene_expr_3stage 6/6 -> 4/6, samoilov_futile_cycle 6/6 -> 7/10, prion_aggregation 104/2809 -> 121/3843. Horizons are unchanged -- they are the manuscript's, not the records'. Prior revision 2026-07-18h: removed the BNGL vilar_circadian (a modified delta_R=0.05 variant); kept the SBML BIOMD35 (published delta_R=0.2).
selection_rule: Every model is (1) published and (2) simulated with exact Gillespie SSA IN ITS SOURCE STUDY, at (3) the published time horizon. Every BNGL model is a curated BNGL-Models record. The three Lin-2019 systems (tcr/erk/prion) are the exact-SSA baseline here and the PSA approximation in Table 7, by design.

provenance_legend.confirmed: source study demonstrably used SSA; reference solid.
provenance_legend.verify: originally-SSA is probable but Bill should confirm the reference / that the source study used SSA.

engine_columns.sbml_note: All three SBML columns are EXACT SSA (bngsim SSA, RoadRunner gillespie, COPASI SSA). Every engine is run on every model; where an engine cannot produce a valid trajectory, its cell is marked N/A with a footnote. Known gap: RoadRunner-gillespie silently does not fire time-triggered events (860/862/864), so those RR cells are expected N/A.

notes: BNGL rows are exact SSA on the pre-generated .net (both engines run the SAME network).

EVERY BNGL row is generated from its curated BNGL-Models record with that record's own generate_network options and every other action stripped; nothing is baked into the seed species afterwards. See ../../models/curated_nets.json for the record, the upstream sha256, and the generated .net sha256.

Horizons are the manuscript's, NOT the records'. Every BNGL row carries record_horizon, the t_end of the record's own active exact-SSA action (null when it declares none), so a row whose horizon was chosen elsewhere says so in the corpus rather than only in prose: mckane_predator_prey and samoilov_futile_cycle run the record's own horizon, gene_bursts (3.6e6), gene_expression (1e8), tcr_signaling (10800), prion_aggregation (10) and gene_expr_3stage (2.1e8) diverge and each says why in its caveats, and erk_activation has no record horizon to compare against. samoilov_futile_cycle used to diverge too, on a value chosen for the superseded model; lanl/bngsim#425 replaced it with the record's.
This file is the corpus SSOT: _ssa_config.py derives every model's file, horizon and n_points from it and adds only runner policy (warm-N, cheap->expensive order, coverage).
Timings are NOT recorded here -- this file defines the CORPUS (models + horizons + provenance). A timing run is a separate step.

SBML inclusion rule: molecule-count encodings ONLY (initialAmount / hasOnlySubstanceUnits=true). Concentration-unit SBML (hasOnlySubstanceUnits=false) is an ODE encoding -- exact SSA on it is ill-posed. Dropped for this reason: Smith2013/474 (ROS went negative) and Karapetyan/586+587.

bngl.name: tcr_signaling
bngl.reference: Lipniacki T, Hat B, Faeder JR, Hlavacek WS (2008) J Theor Biol 254:110-122. Horizon: Lin YT, Feng S, Hlavacek WS (2019) J Chem Phys 150:244101.
caveats: Curated record starts from the integer-rounded endpoint of the paper's 10-hour ligand-free deterministic priming protocol, where the superseded copy started from a clean state. Same 37/97 network, ~3% more Gillespie events at the same horizon.
Horizon t_end=10000 is the Lin-2019 exact-SSA horizon, not the record's own 10800.

bngl.name: erk_activation
bngl.reference: Kochanczyk M, Kocieniewski P, Kozlowska E, Jaruszewicz-Blonska J, Sparta B, Pargett M, Albeck JG, Hlavacek WS, Lipniacki T (2017) Sci Rep 7:38244. Horizon: Lin YT, Feng S, Hlavacek WS (2019) J Chem Phys 150:244101.
caveats: Relabelling, not a re-measurement: the curated record and the superseded copy generate the same 34/65 network with identical seed species and identical effective rate constants (the old copy carried a symbolic system-size parameter lambda=1 and derived _rateLaw* expressions). Measured activity agrees to the event at t_end=86.4.

The record has NO active exact-SSA action -- its only active action is an ODE run at t_end=86400 reproducing Fig. 4B, and its sole stochastic line is a commented-out partial-scaling block. The 8640 horizon comes from Lin et al. (2019).
EXACT SSA IS THE SLOW ANCHOR: populations up to 3e6 -> ~6e8 events/replicate. Feasible; budget for it.
Citation is now the curated record's (with DOI); what is still open is whether the SOURCE STUDY used exact SSA -- hence provenance_status=verify.

bngl.name: prion_aggregation
bngl.reference: Rubenstein R, Gray PC, Cleland TJ, Piltch MS, Hlavacek WS, Roberts RM, Ambrosiano J, Kim J-I (2007) Biophys Chem 125:360-367. Benchmark parameterization and horizon: Lin YT, Feng S, Hlavacek WS (2019) J Chem Phys 150:244101.
caveats: The _benchmark variant of the record (Lin-2019 parameterization, 120-subunit cap). Its generate_network raises max_iter=>150 over BNG's 100-iteration default, so the network reaches the model's own max_stoich=>{PrP=>120} cap: 121 species / 3843 reactions, where the superseded copy froze at 104/2809. The 17 added species are chains of length 104-120, all with zero initial condition, so the event count is unchanged (~605k at t_end=10) but per-event cost rises with the reaction count.
Generation takes ~45 s, most of it isomorphism checking on the longest chains.
Citation is now the curated record's (with DOI); what is still open is whether the SOURCE STUDY used exact SSA -- hence provenance_status=verify.

Horizon t_end=300 is Lin et al. (2019)'s, not the record's own 10. Figure 7 of that paper runs the prion model from 0 to 300 days, so t_end=300 is the published benchmark horizon and the model's time unit is days. The record runs a shorter ten-day trajectory, which is its own choice. Its protocol note used to call that 'the benchmark protocol of Lin et al. (2019)', which was the misattribution; wshlavacek/BNGL-Models#45 corrected it, and this corpus vendors the corrected file. Settled in lanl/bngsim#429.

bngl.name: gene_expr_3stage
caveats: Three-stage single-gene model: DNA(promoter on/off) -> mRNA -> Protein. Small network, very long horizon (t_end=2e8) drives the event count.

4/6, not the 6/6 of the superseded copy: that copy carried a Src() marker and a $Null() sink the curated record does not. Dynamics are unchanged (~6.6e6 events at t_end=2e8, same to within run-to-run noise).
DISTINCT from gene_expression (Munsky) -- single-gene protein cascade vs multi-gene mRNA telegraph.
Horizon t_end=2e8 is the manuscript's; the record's own protocol runs to 2.1e8 and discards the first 1e7 s as burn-in, so the two measure the same 2e8 s window.

bngl.name: gene_expression
bngl.reference: Munsky B, Neuert G, van Oudenaarden A (2012) Science 336:183-187.
caveats: Munsky Fig-2B model: 1 constitutive gene + 3 two-state regulated genes at equal mean but distinct transcript distributions (mRNA-level telegraph).
Same 10/14 network and the same measured activity as the superseded copy.
Horizon t_end=6e4 is the manuscript's; the record's own protocol runs to 1e8.

bngl.name: mckane_predator_prey
bngl.reference: McKane AJ, Newman TJ (2005) Phys Rev Lett 94:218102.
caveats: DEMOGRAPHIC (ecological) stochasticity -- individuals, not molecules. It is exact SSA of a Markov jump process, but ecological rather than biochemical.
Same 3/5 network and the same measured activity as the superseded copy.

bngl.name: gene_bursts
bngl.reference: Lin YT, Doering CR (2016) Phys Rev E 93:022409.
caveats: Coarse-grained bursty gene expression (mRNA + protein). Thematically near gene_expr_3stage / gene_expression but a distinct model.

SEED SPECIES ARE THE ODE STEADY STATE (mRNA=0, Protein=467), produced by the 'relax' step declared for this model in ../../models/curated_nets.json and rounded to whole molecules. The model's protocol -- in the record and in the superseded source alike -- relaxes deterministically and carries that state into the SSA run; it is never simulated stochastically from the bare 0/0 seeds. The relaxation horizon is converged, so the seed is a property of the model, not a free parameter: 3.6e5, 3.6e6 and 3.6e7 s all give the same state, while the record's own 3.6e4 s stops at Protein=111.7, still climbing.

The B07 measurement does NOT move: this .net and the superseded baked copy both give median 923 / mean 930 Gillespie events at t_end=3600 over 200 seeds, with no zero-event replicate. Dropping the relaxation would have made it median 95 with 25 of 200 replicates firing nothing.
Horizon t_end=3600 is one cell cycle, the manuscript's; the record's own protocol runs SSA to 3.6e6 s.

bngl.name: samoilov_futile_cycle
bngl.reference: Samoilov M, Plyasunov S, Arkin AP (2005) PNAS 102:2310-2315.
caveats: Enzymatic futile cycle with noise-induced bistability (Arkin group).

7/10, not the 6/6 of the superseded copy: the curated record is the primary file, with the external noise driver of Expressions 7 and 8 included (the record's _no_driver file is the paper's control, not this study's model).

ROADRUNNER CELL IS N/A: the driver step N + N -> E+ + N is second order in the same species, so the converted SBML law k*N*N is not the exact propensity k*N*(N-1) and RR-gillespie fires the SBML law (GH #9). COPASI is unaffected. The superseded copy had no driver, hence no such reaction and no N/A. The horizon does not enter this: the record's _unordered_pair variant, whose name suggests it addresses the propensity convention, writes the same 5,5 -> 3,5 reaction with the rate constant halved, so the converted law is still k*N*N and the N/A stands for it too.

HORIZON IS THE RECORD'S OWN t_end=10, sampled every 0.005 s, reproducing Fig. 3A. Adopted in lanl/bngsim#425; it replaces t_end=0.0018, which came from the superseded 6/6 from_antimony artifact. That value is not from Samoilov et al. (2005): it is the @SIM annotation of ../../models/antimony/ssys/Samoilov2005.ant, a deterministic ODE encoding kept in a different corpus as a stiffness pathology case for S-system recasting. Two things were wrong with the old pairing. The model had not started: at 0.0018 s the trajectory is still in the burn-in from the Fig. 3 initial condition, with X* down only from 2000 to about 1600 molecules (median 1606 over 30 seeds) against the published operating band of 110-286, which it first reaches at a median 0.0167 s over 30 seeds. And the cell measured almost no simulation: interleaved against a run of the same model that fires zero events, 91% of the bngsim wall and 89% of the run_network wall was per-run fixed overhead. At t_end=10 the row fires a median 1.36e7 events in 0.46 s of bngsim wall and 1.70 s of run_network wall, both far inside the 120 s per-run cap. The B10 cost moves by about four orders of magnitude and the manuscript reports the new number.

engine_coverage.roadrunner: N/A (repeated reactant; RR-gillespie fires k*N*N, not k*N*(N-1))

sbml.title: Proctor2011 - protein homeostasis (high stress)
sbml.reference: Proctor CJ, Lorimer IA (2011) protein homeostasis (Hsp70/Hsp90) -- confirm citation.
caveats: No time-triggered events -- all three engines run it (it is just slow). Run to the FULL horizon (feasible -- the source study ran the full simulation); the parity screen flagged partial_horizon only because of its short wall cap.
CONFIRM the paper's real horizon: the inherited figure-SED-ML value t_end=10 looks short for a proteostasis time course.

sbml.title: Besozzi2012 - oscillatory regimes in the Ras/cAMP/PKA pathway (S. cerevisiae)
sbml.reference: Besozzi D, Cazzaniga P, Pescini D, Mauri G, Colombo S, Martegani E (2012) EURASIP J Bioinform Syst Biol 2012:10. PMID 22818197.
caveats: Model NOTES state it explicitly: 'defined according to the stochastic formulation of chemical kinetics [Gillespie 1977] ... performing stochastic simulations'. Non-Proctor group (Milano-Bicocca stochastic-simulation lab). Adds a signaling-oscillator dimension.
No events/rules -> all three engines run it. DIFF in the screen was partial_horizon (wall cap); run to the full paper horizon.
sbml.t_end_status: PLACEHOLDER -- the parity-screen horizon, not Besozzi 2012's. Confirm from the paper before the final run.

sbml.title: Vilar2002 - circadian oscillator (molecule-count SBML)
sbml.reference: Vilar JMG, Kueh HY, Barkai N, Leibler S (2002) Mechanisms of noise-resistance in genetic oscillators. PNAS 99:5988-5992.
caveats: Molecule-count encoding (hasOnlySubstanceUnits=true for all 10 species; DA=DR=1, rest 0) -- passes the SSA molecule-count rule; runs clean (no negative species).

The BNGL twin (vilar_circadian) was REMOVED: it differed in exactly one rate constant -- repressor degradation delta_R = 0.05 (written 0.2/4 in the RuleHub source) vs the published Vilar-2002 value 0.2 used here. All 14 other rate constants and the 16-reaction network are identical. This SBML is the faithful encoding.
Non-Proctor -- one of two non-Proctor SBML rows (with Besozzi/478).
